AGENDA
  GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  COUNCIL CHAMBER, City Hall – 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206

  OCTOBER 7, 2019
  4:00 PM

  1. ROLL CALL

  2. CONSENT ITEMS
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the Commission or the audience requesting separate
  consideration may do so by making such request before motion is proposed.

  a. Approval of the minutes for the September 5, 2019 Special Meeting

  3. GWP COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS

  4. REPORTS - INFORMATION
  a. Customer Services Update
  b. Electrical System Summer Performance

  5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS (5) Minutes
  Discussion is limited to items NOT part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five (5) minutes – Commission may question or
  respond to the speaker, but there will be no debate or decision. The General Manager may refer the matter to appropriate staff for
  investigation and report.

  6. AGENDA FORECAST

  7. ADJOURNMENT

  Next Meeting is scheduled for November 4, 2019

Welcome to the meeting of the Glendale Water & Power Commission. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast throughout the week.
Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office by calling (818) 548-2090. Meetings are also
archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at www.ci.glendale.ca.us/video_archives.asp. PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES AND PAGERS WHILE
INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon
request. Assisted listening devices are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for requests regarding sign
language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the GWP Administration Office 141 N. Glendale Avenue 4th Floor, Glendale, CA 91206. If you have any
question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact Catalina Lee (818) 548-2107 during regular business hours.
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  MEETING OF THE GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  COUNCIL CHAMBER, City Hall – 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206

  October 7, 2019
  4:00 PM

1. ROLL CALL
  Present: President Avanessian, Commissioners Carrasco, Kedikian, Lall and Watson

2. CONSENT ITEMS
  a. Approval of the September 5, 2019 Special Meeting Minutes
  Motion to Approve as Amended (under “GWP Commission/ Staff Comments,” in line 5 of the first paragraph,
  changed “her” to “his”):
  Moved by: Commissioner Lall
  Seconded by: Commissioner Watson
  Motion Passed.

3. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  General Manager Steve Zurn and each of the Commissioners thanked Commissioner Watson for his service and
  wished him well. Commissioner Watson stated that he regretted that his time on the Commission was short, as he
  is moving out of state. He thanked his fellow Commissioners, expressed his gratitude for the opportunity to learn
  about the workings of the utility, and praised GWP for excellent service.

4. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. Customer Services Update. Ms. Tami Vallier, Customer Services Administrator, provided a first quarter
  customer services update, focused on recent accomplishments, current projects, highlights, and customer service
  metrics.

  Ms. Vallier responded to questions from the Commission. She clarified that GWP’s average talk time target is
  realistic and achievable under normal circumstances, and typical for the industry, but average talk time can increase
  when GWP rolls out new programs, and GWP customer service representatives are encouraged to take the time
  needed to respond to questions about those programs. Ms. Vallier confirmed that during an outage call center
  targets are thrown off and a different target might be appropriate. Ms. Vallier and Mr. Zurn stated that the trend
  toward increased requests for field service and increased inquiries is a good thing, as this shows that customers are
  engaging with GWP programs and looking at ways to save water and energy, such as through GWP’s leak alert
  program.

  b. Electrical System Summer Performance. Mr. Zurn reported on the electrical system’s performance including
  the July 24, 2019 outage and subsequent repairs. He stated that the loss was caused by the failure of an auxiliary
  transformer, which triggered an outage of the main transformer and cascaded to other substations. Mr. Zurn stated
  this was an N-1-1 event on our distribution system. He expressed gratitude to GWP’s crews, who worked around
  the clock to complete the repairs and respond to customer inquiries, to LADWP for assisting with repairs and
  Burbank Water & Power for supplying wire to complete the repairs.
   In response to questions from the Commission, Mr. Zurn confirmed transformer is now repaired. Even with the
  “Clean Energy RFP” solutions implemented, Mr. Zurn stated it would not have helped or prevented against this
  outage, because we had sufficient supply of energy, but lost our ability to distribute it. Mr. Zurn agreed with
  Commissioners that communications during and after an outage are important. Mr. Zurn stated he is proud of
  GWP’s customer service representatives who worked tirelessly to respond to questions, and GWP will continue to
  improve its outage-related notifications. Mr. Zurn stated that GWP provided a post-outage briefing to the City
  Council on September 10, and has been updating the public via social media and on the GWP website. With regard
  to inventory, Mr. Zurn stated that GWP considers its historic need for supplies, lead time to acquire supplies, and
  whether other utilities may stock items. He stated that GWP traditionally does not stock transformers and bushings,
  but may reconsider its strategy. Mr. Zurn noted that transformers are an expensive ($1 million) item to keep on a
  shelf, but can have a long lead time. With respect to other items, Mr. Zurn stated that GWP is pretty well taken care
  of. President Avanessian recommended a power system reliability study. Mr. Zurn responded that GWP will
  consider incorporating this into its planning, as GWP is putting together a master plan for capital assets, including
  the plan for its poles approaching the end of their lifespan.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None.

6. AGENDA FORECAST
  Commissioners Lall and Carrasco requested an update on the Clean Energy RFP. Mr. Zurn stated that discussions are
  moving along with the Clean Energy RFP vendors and recommended discussing the appropriate timing for such a report
  during the agenda forecast discussions in early 2020. Mr. Zurn stated that he anticipated a more substantive report could
  occur in the spring of 2020.

  No changes were made to the proposed agenda forecasts for future meetings.

7. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Watson
  Seconded by: Commissioner Kedikian
  Motion Passed.
  The meeting was adjourned at 4:49 p.m.
